previous_plan_experience.tactical_thesis: Plan A's merged-anchor idea survives, but the frame 0-941 opening must be rebuilt on three corrections. (1) The [8,5] pocket holder is a block-1 merchant (talr primary, nothin mirror) whose basic attacks are part of the fire plan, because the only block-2 candidate (wscoot) neither blocks nor attacks without a manual skill it cannot ready before route-1 leaks at 219 (S1 earliest ready = deploy+240 even from a frame-0 deploy). (2) The anchor is caper locked at [9,2] facing DOWN (the only verified coverage of [8,5]; angel/aprl are geometrically excluded), funded by natural regen at frame ~390 (ledger: 10+13-11=12.0 DP, zero refund assumed). Frame 250 is abandoned as a deadline: it was an artifact of the 13-DP prefix plus caper-only plus continuous-hold assumptions, and is unaffordable under ANY prefix that also blocks route-1 (it would allow at most 1.33 DP of pre-anchor spending beyond the stub). Instead, route-1's <805 contract is certified redundantly (caper-only from any establishment <=474 gives kill at first-attack+330; talr solo kills at ~500 regardless), and route-3's <941 contract is certified by holder cooperation (~641 eDPS combined, kill ~600-660) inside the 431-459 block window, with a budgeted concession if cooperation cannot be certified. (3) A05/route-6 is conceded by default: two simultaneous duelist slots cannot be filled by one live talr, strong is on redeploy cooldown (~390 to ~1140), and wscoot is disqualified - the concession is structural, not economic, and does not depend on the refund UNKNOWN. All merchant exposure is bounded (<=2 concurrent, retreat-on-job-done), and every claim depending on refund, upkeep, roadblock legality, target ordering or client timing is quarantined into conditional branches with life-budget fallbacks (default 2 leaks of 5; worst certified case 3; absolute worst under real upkeep 4, margin >=1).
